event: The racer's countdown goes off for nobody; its wheel jerks on its own for a ghost car.
Aura flipped it to attract mode an hour ago; Awen has looked at it four times.
Its steering column has a dead spot four degrees left, and Awen keeps not mentioning it.
Aura, at the change counter over the takeout, says Awen is making the face at her machine.
"It has a dead spot." "It's had a dead spot since before you."
The room is dark but for the cabinets: red off the racer, cold blue off the rhythm cab.
The rhythm cab's marquee light still ticks at its ballast, as it has for months.
Awen calls it not a defense but a timeline, and crosses to Aura.
Aura passes the chopsticks back over her shoulder without looking; Awen takes them blind.
Awen steals from the gutted carton on principle; the first one opened is fought over.
Aura sets a pre-emptive house rule: dumplings stay off the Street Fighter cab.
Awen turns her bag so the twice-taped corner of the thing inside doesn't show.
She won't hand it over yet; the evening still has ornament on it.
Aura came round the counter at half her usual speed, and Awen clocked it silently.
Awen lets her carry whatever it is until she's ready to set it down.
Aura challenges her to the racer: Awen is down two in the room.
Aura drops into the good left seat; loser has the last dumpling taken at her choosing.
Awen eyes the right seat's wheel; she could fix the four degrees in ten minutes.
She sets the carton down and gets in anyway.
The light-tree drops green and Aura is a whole car-length gone on the ghost-line.
Awen drives the wheel she's got, feeding the correction in early before each corner.
Slower on paper but honest, it gains her about a length a lap.
Aura, eyes on the road, says she can hear Awen doing something over there.
"Driving." Aura calls it her fixing-my-machine-with-your-face sound.
Awen takes the hairpin, hands four degrees ahead: she's just being polite to it.
Aura's shoulder drops a half-inch on the straight; Awen files it and keeps her line.
Awen comes out of the chicane closer than she went in.
Aura says Artemis drove like Awen, never meeting a straight shot she wouldn't complicate.
"You didn't have cars." "Chariots. Same principle, worse suspension."
The gap shrinks; Aura says Artemis would have loved Awen, and it'd be unbearable.
Aura takes the last corner flat-out on the greedy ghost-line.
Her line runs one hair wide at exit, leaving a gap one car wide on the inside.
Awen is already in it and draws level at the line.
"That didn't happen." Aura is out of the seat before the replay finishes.
The photo-finish gives it to the inside car by a bumper.
Awen stays at the wheel: it's on the board and will keep saying the same thing.
"You drove the broken one." "I drove the one nobody else wanted. That's just manners."
Aura taps the cabinet twice, a private thing between machine and owner.
She invokes the sulk: one song's length, and Awen may not talk to her during it.
Awen says she wrote that rule to have a legal way to lose; Aura: because she's a genius.
Aura drifts toward the rhythm cab to pick a song loud enough to be a statement.
She says the dumpling is still Awen's: she pays her debts, just resentfully.
Awen calls it one of her best qualities; Aura says it's her worst and best at once.
At the rhythm cab Aura lays her hand flat on the panel and doesn't start it.
For one whole second she stands with her back to Awen, reading the flicker.
Awen watches the back of her not start the song.
Aura says "Hey, so—" at normal speed, stops, and folds the real sentence away.
Instead, faster: Awen will want to sit down for how badly Aura's about to lose to her.
"You said no talking during the sulk." "The sulk hasn't started. I haven't picked the song."
She jabs the panel and the cabinet wakes loud, a four-on-the-floor song with too many arrows.
She rolls her shoulders: now the sulk has started; Awen is to come over and lose politely.
